name: Four Centuries of Sound: The Classical Masterpieces
description: A listener's guide to the works of Bach, Mozart, Beethoven and beyond, from the Baroque, Classical and Romantic periods to the early modern music of Debussy, Stravinsky and Ravel.

checkpoints.name: The Baroque
checkpoints.note: Courts and churches pay composers for rich, ornate music, and Bach, Handel and Vivaldi write concertos, oratorios and fugues that are still played daily.

checkpoints.name: The Classical period
checkpoints.note: Clear tunes and balanced forms dominate in Vienna, and Mozart and the young Beethoven turn the symphony and the sonata into serious art.

checkpoints.name: The Romantic century
checkpoints.note: Feeling takes first place. Orchestras grow larger, and composers write about nations, nature and the inner self, including Beethoven's last symphony.

checkpoints.name: Towards the modern
checkpoints.note: Composers look for new colours and rhythms. Debussy paints with sound and Stravinsky shocks a Paris crowd with a ballet score.

checkpoints.name: Jazz, ballet and the new century
checkpoints.note: Jazz, dance and film change the concert hall, and works by Gershwin, Ravel and Orff reach an audience beyond it.
